notes:
Prospect: mid-market KM SaaS (B2B) focused on enterprise knowledge search and summarization. Evaluating Redwood for embeddings + semantic search. Wants hosted API initially for speed to market; roadmap to Dedicated for predictable throughput and lower per-token cost. 

Key asks from demo/calls: quick proof that hosted embeddings can meet nightly batch throughput (target ~1M embeddings/day) and that realtime search latencies p95 <200ms end-to-end. Preference to integrate with their Postgres+pgvector pipeline but open to managed vector DBs (Pinecone/Redis). Security: must provide SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML for admin console, audit logs, and optional EU data residency for customers. 

Quote from CTO on 2026-02-15 call: "We need predictable economics for embedding refresh jobs — spikes are expensive today." AE/Jordan: emphasized Dedicated reserved pools and Optimize tooling for batching suggestions. SE/Morgan demoed hosted embeddings + redirect to pgvector in a 2-day spike test. 

POC approach agreed (high-level): week-1: ingest 200k historical docs via hosted API batching + ETL; week-2: measure end-to-end search latency and recall vs baseline; week-3-4: scale to 1M/day batch job and test fallback to quantized open models to compare cost. Decision criteria: latency, cost per 1M embeddings, ease of vector DB integration, SLA for p95. 

CRM shorthand: trial credits issued 2026-02-20; demo recording in Drive; legal sent NDA + standard T&Cs; waiting on procurement budget line.

Need both low-latency realtime queries and high-throughput offline embedding pipelines.

Latency: search end-to-end p95 <200ms; embedding p95 <150ms when called realtime

Batching: ability to run optimized multi-threaded batch uploads with checkpoint/resume
Model choices: prefer cost-efficient open models with option to fall back to smaller quantized variants
Monitoring: token-level cost and latency per route; audit logs for all admin actions
